grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: peak near 21% relative proportion at a few µm with a tail up to ~100 µm

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed polygonal grains crossed by long straight parallel annealing-twin lamellae; grain size larger than S950
phases_present.texture: random crystallographic orientation distribution (no significant preferred orientation)

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) austenitic structure with recrystallized equiaxed grains, abundant annealing twin boundaries (ATBs, Σ3, 60°) and high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, >10°); no significant preferred orientation.

unmapped_findings: S1050 surface corrosion morphology after potentiodynamic polarization to 5 mA/cm²: three isolated corrosion pits, with one magnified inset showing a dark irregular pit with a bright halo (Fig. 7c, b0041).
S1050 EIS Nyquist plot shows a single capacitive arc intermediate between S950 (largest) and S0 (smallest), with S1050 and S1150 falling between (Fig. 8, b0042).

S1050 Al content in the surface oxide film is approximately just below 80 at% (read from Fig. 14); the precise printed value is not given, while S950 is 90.17 at% and S1150 is 69.91 at% (b0075, b0132).
S1050 grain-size histogram (Fig. 4c): peak near 21% relative proportion at a few µm with a tail up to ~100 µm; average grain size 21.1 µm.
S1050 Rp versus immersion time (Fig. 18): plateaus near 8×10⁴ Ω·cm² after ~24 h (no numeric label printed for S1050; text gives S950 = 114.9 kΩ·cm² and S1150 = 50.6 kΩ·cm² at 168 h).
S1050 second-cycle CV shows substantially enhanced Fe/Mn anodic peak near -0.56 V_SCE compared with S950, indicating an incompletely formed surface film (b0123).
Solution treatment at 1050 °C dissolves the κ-carbide precipitates present in the as-hot-rolled S0 condition (alloy snapshot; b0038 shows κ-carbides only in S0).
